title: The failed campaign toward Jerusalem
summary: Rezin and Pekah went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.

explicit_facts.text: Rezin was king of Syria.
Pekah, son of Remaliah, was king of Israel.
Rezin and Pekah went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.

unspecified_visual_details: Their appearance, clothing, weapons, the number of people accompanying them, and Jerusalem's architecture are not specified.

narration.text: Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah the son of Remaliah, king of Israel, went up toward Jerusalem to war against it, but could not prevail against it.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Jerusalem being captured or invent a specific battle or retreat.

title: A report to the house of David
summary: The house of David is told that Syria is confederate with Ephraim. His heart and the heart of his people are moved.

The precise location and appearance of those who receive it.

narration.text: And it was told the house of David, saying:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The trees moved by wind are a comparison, not a separate narrated event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the report's speaker or replace “his” with an unsupported name.
Do not assign a precise location or a more specific identity to his people.
Do not depict literal trees or wind as the cause of the reaction.

title: A Warning Not to Fear
summary: An unidentified speaker directs someone to tell another person not to fear the fierce anger of Rezin with Syria and the son of Remaliah.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker directs someone to tell another person to take heed, be quiet, and not fear or be faint-hearted.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The smoking firebrands are figurative language, not literal objects.

summary: Isaiah recounts the evil counsel of Syria, Ephraim, and the son of Remaliah to attack Judah and install the son of Tabeal as king.

unspecified_visual_details: The participants in the reported counsel and where it took place.

title: The Lord God’s declaration and warning
summary: The Lord God says it will not stand or come to pass, identifies the heads of Syria, Damascus, Ephraim, and Samaria, foretells Ephraim’s breaking within three score and five years, and warns that those who will not believe will not be established.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord God says it will not stand or come to pass.
Damascus is the head of Syria, and Rezin is the head of Damascus.
Ephraim is foretold to be broken within three score and five years so that it will not be a people.
Samaria is the head of Ephraim, and Remaliah’s son is the head of Samaria.
The warning says that those who will not believe will not be established.

unspecified_visual_details: The setting, audience, and appearance of any messenger are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: For the head of Syria is Damascus, and the head of Damascus, Rezin; and within three score and five years shall Ephraim be broken that it be not a people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lord God

spoken_dialogue.text: And the head of Ephraim is Samaria, and the head of Samaria is Remaliah’s son. If ye will not believe surely ye shall not be established.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Lord God

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Ephraim’s breaking is foretold, not narrated as an event occurring in this scene.
The Lord God is identified as the source of the words; these verses do not describe a visible appearance.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Ephraim’s foretold breaking as a present event.
Do not identify an addressee or a human messenger from these verses.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord God.

title: The sign of Immanuel
summary: An unidentified speaker addresses the house of David and asks whether it is a small thing to weary men and whether they will weary his God also. He says the Lord will give a sign: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, who shall eat butter and honey to know to refuse evil and choose good.

explicit_facts.text: A speaker addresses the house of David and asks whether they will weary his God as well as men.
The speaker says the Lord himself shall give a sign: a virgin shall conceive, bear a son, and call his name Immanuel.
The son shall eat butter and honey so that he may know to refuse evil and choose good.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The speaker may be depicted addressing listeners, without identifying any individual listener.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity and appearance.
The listeners' appearances and number.

spoken_dialogue.text: O house of David; is it a small thing for you to weary men, but will ye weary my God also?
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The speaker says the Lord will give the sign; the verse does not depict the Lord speaking.

title: The land forsaken by its kings
summary: The speaker foretells that the land will be forsaken by both its kings before the child knows to refuse evil and choose good. The Lord will bring days unlike those since Ephraim departed from Judah upon the person addressed, that person's people, and that person's father's house. The king of Assyria is mentioned.

explicit_facts.text: Before the child knows to refuse evil and choose good, the land the addressee abhors will be forsaken by both its kings.

unspecified_visual_details: The speaker's identity, appearance, and surroundings are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: For before the child shall know to refuse the evil and choose the good, the land that thou abhorrest shall be forsaken of both her kings.

spoken_dialogue.text: The Lord shall bring upon thee, and upon thy people, and upon thy father’s house, days that have not come from the day that Ephraim departed from Judah, the king of Assyria.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unknown speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Both verses foretell future events rather than narrate those events taking place.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the kings leaving the land or the foretold days as present events.
Do not assign the king of Assyria a role beyond what the wording establishes.

summary: In that day, the Lord shall hiss for the fly in Egypt and the bee in Assyria. They shall come and rest in desolate valleys, holes of rocks, thorns, and bushes.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord shall hiss for the fly in the uttermost part of Egypt and the bee in Assyria.

unspecified_visual_details: The terrain's precise appearance and lighting.

And they shall come, and shall rest all of them in the desolate valleys, and in the holes of the rocks, and upon all thorns, and upon all bushes.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Present this as a future prophecy, not a present-tense event.

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict human armies or give the Lord an invented visible appearance.
